---
title: "Module 11 --- Wet testing"
---

## Summary

Immersion, underwater runs, wing and tail trim, and a logged cost-of-transport measurement.

## Requirements

|  |  |
|------------------------------------|------------------------------------|
| **Bring** | Fully waterproofed robot from [Module 10](10-waterproofing.qmd), charged 4S pack, spare crank–linkage shaft |
| **Tools** | Retrieval poles and towels are at the tank --- see [Tank rules](#the-tank) |
| **Read** | This page, the notes from [Module 4](04-control.qmd), and [Cost of transport](/reference/cost-of-transport.qmd) |

## Pre-immersion flight checks

- [ ] Red charging connector closed.
- [ ] USB-C port sealed.
- [ ] Watchdog enabled on the ESC (`W`) - target drops to zero if commands stop

## After immersion

- [ ] Check for water in the two connectors
- [ ] Rinse the bearings with Isopropyl Alcohol.

## The tank and tracking system {#the-tank}

Testing happens in the AURA Lab tank. The ceiling camera tracks the robot for the cost-of-transport number below.

![The AURA Lab tank. The rail and gantry run the length of the near side; the tracking cameras are mounted overhead.](/Fig/AURALabTank.jpg){#fig-tank width="100%"}

::: callout-warning
## Tank rules

**Nobody gets in the tank.** Not to retrieve a robot, not to reposition it, not for a moment. Use the **poles** to fish the robot back to the edge.

**Keep water off the floor.** Water on the floor sets off an alarm, which ends the session for everyone. Lift the robot out over the tank and let it drain there rather than carrying it dripping, and keep **towels** to hand for what gets past. Dry the floor immediately if it happens.
:::

## What data your robot should log

Every run should record, at minimum:

- **Power consumption** --- the numerator of cost of transport
- **IMU data** --- attitude and acceleration through the run
- **Flapping frequency**

Since underwater we lose wireless communication, the data needs to be recorded and streamed back wirelessly after the run. There are two places to record data on the flight controller, and the choice matters more than it looks:

|                     | **RAM**         | **Flash**                              |
|------------------------|------------------------|------------------------|
| Survives power loss | No              | Yes                                    |
| Speed               | Fast, no wear   | Slower, finite write cycles            |
| Use it for          | The normal case | Runs that cannot afford to be repeated |

The normal workflow is **log to RAM during the run, then broadcast over BLE once the robot is out of the water**. Nothing has to be opened and nothing has to be plugged in, which is the whole point: the board is potted from [Module 10](10-waterproofing.qmd) and there is no connector to reach.

::: callout-warning
## RAM is lost the moment power goes

A brownout, a watchdog reset, or an accidental disconnect takes the whole run with it. Broadcast the data before changing the battery, not after - and if a run is expensive to repeat, write it to flash instead.
:::

## Robot trim

Two independent adjustments, both mechanical. Change **one at a time** with a run between them, otherwise there is no telling which one did what. Wing trim is typically adjusted at the **trailing edge**. Tail trim is manual: **bend and twist the tail by hand**. Bending sets pitch, twisting sets roll. Work in small increments and expect to go back and forth - there is no scale and no reference mark, so the logged runs are the only feedback available.

Robot needs to float level. If not, add floats (foam, 3D-print).

## Cost of transport

Cost of transport is the score in [Module 12](12-competition.qmd). How it is defined and how to measure it - power from the robot's log, speed from the ceiling cameras - is on the [Cost of transport](/reference/cost-of-transport.qmd) reference page. Read it before your first scored run.

::: callout-note
## Checkpoint

A completed underwater run with power logged and successfully retrieved over BLE, no water ingress on inspection afterwards, and a cost-of-transport figure computed as on the [Cost of transport](/reference/cost-of-transport.qmd) page, with the camera-derived speed.
:::
